name: Kansas

ks-25-3108.citation: K.S.A. 25-3108 (tie votes in elections of local officers)

ks-25-3208.citation: K.S.A. 25-3208 (tie votes in state and national elections)

ks-25-3209.citation: K.S.A. 25-3209 (tie vote for governor and lieutenant governor; determination by legislature)

ks-25-3107.citation: K.S.A. 25-3107 (procedure for canvass by county board; recount, when; recount procedure; payment of costs)

ties.applies_to: any election for which the state board of canvassers makes the final canvass: a tie for a national or state office, in a primary (for candidates of the same party) or a general election, except the general election for governor and lieutenant governor
ties.steps: the state board of canvassers determines by lot which person is nominated or elected; reasonable notice is given to the tied persons, and the board proceeds in their absence if they fail to appear; a tie has occurred when two or more persons have an equal number of votes and more than any other person for the same office

sources.quote: In any election for which the state board of canvassers makes the final canvass, if any two or more persons have a tie vote, such board shall determine by lot which person is nominated or elected, as the case may be, except in general election of the governor and lieutenant governor.
In a general election for any national or state office, if any two or more persons have an equal number of votes and more than any other person for the same office.
In a primary election for any national or state office, if any two or more persons have an equal number of votes and more than any other person for the same office as candidate for the same party.

ties.note: State legislative seats are read as 'state office' [inferred]; the section does not name legislators. For a national office, whether a tie has occurred follows any applicable federal statutes (25-3208(b)(3)).

ties.applies_to: the office of president and vice president, a national office, in a general election
ties.steps: read through the rule for national offices: the state board of canvassers determines the tie by lot, subject to any federal statutes on whether a tie has occurred

sources.quote: In the case of election to any national office determination of whether a tie has occurred shall be made and such determination shall be based upon any federal statutes applicable to the particular national office, if there be any such federal statutes, and in all other respects according to this section.
(B) the office of president or vice president of the United States; (C) the office of members of the United States house of representatives;

ties.note: The statutes name the office of president or vice president (25-3107) and national offices (25-3208); no section read names presidential electors. That the tie rule reaches the presidential contest is the reader's reading [inferred].

ties.applies_to: a general election for governor and lieutenant governor in which two or more pairs of candidates running together are tied
ties.steps: the two houses determine the election by joint ballot; the president of the senate and the speaker of the house deposit a certificate with the secretary of state showing who was elected
ties.who: the two houses of the legislature, by joint ballot

sources.quote: the two houses shall, by joint ballot, determine the election.

ties.applies_to: county and township offices in a primary or general election; city and school offices as the county board determines under the statutes applicable to those elections
ties.steps: the county board of canvassers determines by lot which person is nominated or elected; reasonable notice is given to the tied persons, and the board proceeds in their absence if they fail to appear; for city and school offices the county board decides whether a tie has occurred under the statutes applicable to the particular election

sources.quote: In any election for which the county board of canvassers makes the final canvass, if any two or more persons have a tie vote, such board shall determine by lot which person is nominated or elected, as the case may be.
In a primary election for any county or township office, if any two or more persons have an equal number of votes and more than any other person for the same office as candidate for the same party.

In the case of election to any city office determination of whether a tie has occurred shall be made by the county board of canvassers, and such determination shall be based upon statutes applicable to the particular city election and the number of votes received by the candidates.

ties.note: State general law only; city and school election statutes (which decide whether a tie has occurred) were not read and charters were not read.

ties.applies_to: a question submitted election, a constitutional amendment or other question
ties.steps: a tie is never deemed to have occurred; if there are the same number of yes votes and no votes, the no vote prevails (except, for state questions, on the retention of a justice of the supreme court; for local questions, unless otherwise provided by law)

sources.quote: In the case of a constitutional amendment or other question submitted election a tie shall never be deemed to have occurred, and if there are the same number of "yes" votes and "no" votes, the "no" votes shall have prevailed, except in the case of a question upon the retention of a justice of the supreme court.

In the case of a question submitted election a tie shall never be deemed to have occurred, and if there are the same number of "yes" votes and "no" votes, the "no" vote shall have prevailed unless otherwise provided by law.

ties.note: The statute provides no lot or new election for a question; an equal vote means the question fails. For a retention question the statute leaves the rule to other law, which was not read.

threshold.conditions: written request filed with the county election officer not later than 5 p.m. on the day following the last meeting of the county board of canvassers; the request names the voting areas to be recounted; the recount is completed by 5 p.m. on the fifth day after the request; the requester files a bond (security approved by the county or district attorney) conditioned to pay all costs incurred by the county
threshold.in_words: any candidate may request a recount of all or specified voting areas for the office, and any registered elector who voted in a question submitted election may request a recount, whatever the margin, on a bond for the costs

who_may_request: any candidate, for the office for which the person is a candidate
any registered elector who cast a ballot in a question submitted election
a majority of the county board of canvassers may itself order one for manifest errors on the face of the poll books
recounts.cost_bearer: the requester, by bond; if the requesting candidate is declared the winner, or if a question is overturned, no action is taken on the bond and the county bears the costs

sources.quote: or if any candidate shall request the recount of the ballots cast in all or in only specified voting areas for the office for which the person is a candidate, or if any registered elector who cast a ballot in a question submitted election requests a recount in all or only specified voting areas to determine the result of the election

the party who makes the request shall file with the county election officer a bond, with security to be approved by the county or district attorney, conditioned to pay all costs incurred by the county in making the recount.
Any recount must be requested in writing and filed with the county election officer not later than 5 p.m. on the day following the last meeting of the county board of canvassers.

recounts.note: Subsection (b) is the general rule, in the county's own canvass; offices and questions covered by subsections (c) and (d) (statewide, national, the legislature and the state board of education, and constitutional amendments) are recorded in the rules below. 'No margin required' is the reader's reading of the absence of a margin condition [as written]. There is no automatic recount in 25-3107.

threshold.conditions: applies to a state or national office elected on a statewide basis, president or vice president, U.S. House, a state senate or house member whose district is in two or more counties, the state board of education, and a constitutional amendment; request in writing to the secretary of state not later than 5 p.m. on the day following the last meeting of the county board of canvassers canvassing the election, naming counties or precincts; the recount is completed by 5 p.m. on the fifth day after the request
threshold.in_words: any candidate may request a recount in one or more counties, and any registered elector who voted on a constitutional amendment may, whatever the margin, on a bond set by the secretary of state

who_may_request: any registered elector who cast a ballot in an election for a constitutional amendment
recounts.cost_bearer: the requester, by a bond whose amount the secretary of state determines; if the requesting candidate is declared the winner, no action is taken on the bond and the counties bear the costs (a legislative or state board of education candidate may post the county-type bond instead)

sources.quote: Any candidate may request a recount in one or more counties.

the person requesting the recount shall file, contemporaneously with a request for a recount, a bond with the secretary of state, with security to be approved by the secretary of state, conditioned to pay all costs incurred by the counties and the secretary of state in making the recount.

In the event that the candidate requesting the recount is declared the winner of the election as a result of the recount, no action shall be taken on the candidate's bond and the counties shall bear the costs incurred for the recount.

recounts.note: Subsection (c). The subsection's own list of offices (its (c)(1)) was read; primaries are read as covered because the section speaks of 'candidate' and 'election' generally and the county subsection names nominations [inferred]. Presidential electors are read through 'the office of president or vice president' [inferred].

threshold.percent_of: the total number of votes cast
threshold.conditions: a candidate defeated in a general election for a state or national office elected on a statewide basis, president or vice president, U.S. House, state senate or house, or the state board of education; the candidate requests a recount in one or more counties; no bond is required and the state bears the cost of a recount by the method by which the ballots were counted originally
threshold.in_words: a candidate defeated by one-half of one percent or less of the total votes cast may request a recount in one or more counties at the state's expense, with no bond

recounts.cost_bearer: the state (no bond), for a recount by the method used in the original count; counties are reimbursed their necessary direct expenses through the secretary of state

sources.quote: (d) (1) The provisions of this subsection shall apply to any general elections for: (A) Any state or national office elected on a statewide basis; (B) the office of president or vice president of the United States; (C) the office of members of the United States house of representatives; (D) the office of members of [...] state senate or house of representatives; and (E) the office of members of the state board of education.

Whenever the election returns reflect that a candidate for office was defeated by ½ of 1% or less of the total number of votes cast and if the candidate requests a recount in one or more counties, no bond shall be required and the state shall bear the cost of any recount performed using the method by which the ballots were counted originally.

recounts.note: Subsection (d). It is a recount on request at the state's cost within the margin, not an automatic one; beyond the margin the requester posts a bond under subsection (c). Measures are not covered by (d). 'Total number of votes cast' is the text's base.

unread.what: city and school election statutes that decide whether a tie has occurred in city and school offices, the statutes on presidential electors, recounts of retention questions, and the election contest chapters
unread.reason: not read; 25-3108 sends these to the statutes applicable to the particular election, and contests are litigation (brief)

notes: Kansas was read at the Revisor of Statutes' site: the chapter 25 contents page, sections 25-3107, 25-3108, 25-3203, 25-3208 and 25-3209. Ties go by lot (a tie for governor and lieutenant governor by joint ballot of the two houses, a tie on a question fails); no recount is automatic; a candidate defeated by one-half of one percent or less in a general election for a statewide, national, legislative or state board of education office gets a recount at the state's cost on request.
Section 25-3107's page prints the Revisor's note that the word 'the' was left out of (d)(1)(D); the quotation keeps the page's footnote asterisks cut with [...].
